newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Blochs details minority, standby offer.
newsitem.headline: Blochs details minority, standby offer.

text.p: Blochs Ltd said on Friday that a consortium which had bought a controlling stake in the firm would make an offer to minority shareholders of 107.0 cents per share for their holdings.

However, as this amount, which was based on the net asset value per Bloch share, was well below the firm's recent share price on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange since the announcement of the deal, a standby offer would be made to shareholders.
This offer would, however, only become operative should Bloch's shares fall below 107.0 cents in which case a further announcement would be made.

Since the news earlier this month that a consortium, including Jeffrey Livingstone and Chester Industries Ltd, will buy a controlling stake in the supermarket outfit, Blochs shares have traded between 140 and 184 cents.

The consortium said that it was in the process of identifying suitable assets for Blochs to buy and an announcement would be made once agreement had been reached. It said that no acquisition was imminent but that it intended to buy assets prior to the suspension of Bloch's listing on December 14, 1997.
Shareholders were advised to exercise caution in their sharedealings.
